rv.q: It is a breathtaking debut from a major new playwright, a triumph of direction and design, and a showcase for two performances of extraordinary depth.
Camping is their tragedy, a shattering off-Broadway debut from a playwright to watch.
This is the first professional production of playwright Victoria Lynne Barclay, and it is a strong start out of the gate.

Minifie and Kremelberg’s chemistry feels genuine: you never doubt that they know each other better than anyone else ever will, and yet we can also always see the spark that Ari is trying to flame and Brit to smother.
The forward momentum feels assured from first scene to last, as though the playwright and director know exactly where it’s going and trust us to keep up.

cn.t: Critics praise this impressive debut as a haunting two-hander that traces 25 years of female friendship within the confines of a tent, with strong performances elevating an intimate exploration of how adolescent selves shape adult lives.
